Photograph: Wason Wanichakorn/AP View image in fullscreen Friends of an injured school teacher, who has been carried into the ambulance, embrace at the site of a school shooting, in Thailand's Nonthaburi province. Photograph: Wason Wanichakorn/AP Thailand Thailand school shooting toll rises to nine after 12-year-old dies, police say Teenage girl treated in hospital after Friday’s school shooting has died, police say Staff and agencies Sat 8 Aug 2026 22.11 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 02.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The death toll from a school shooting in Thailand rose to nine on Saturday, after police said a 12-year-old girl caught up in Friday’s incident had died. Police at the Plai Bang Police Station in Nonthaburi Province said the girl, who had been treated at hospital with critical wounds, had died, a day after a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot his grandparents and then killed more people at his school before turning the gun on ⁠himself. Thailand school shooting: eight killed including suspected attacker, police say Read more The 14-year-old wounded more than 30 people in the ⁠shooting at the Debsirin Nonthaburi school northwest of Bangkok. Fourteen people remained in hospital on Saturday evening, seven of them in critical condition. Police are questioning more witnesses as part of their investigation, including the suspect’s parents. The boy had lived with his grandparents for 12 years after his parents had separated, Atthapol Anusit, deputy commissioner of the Provincial Police Region 1, ‌told reporters on Sunday. The suspected attacker fired at least 26 bullets with a gun belonging to his grandfather, and was found with 34 additional ammunition rounds. Police on Sunday told reporters the teenager had an air ⁠gun confiscated by a teacher last year and had watched violent content online and used social media to learn how to ⁠use a firearm. “According to witness interviews, the perpetrator had begun showing interest in ​studying the use of firearms ‌for some time, about one ‌to two years,” Atthapol said. Atthapol, who said police had so far interviewed 17 witnesses, said a knife had also been found in the boy’s bag and other evidence found at the crime scenes included a firearm, spent cartridge cases, and a personal computer. On the day of the incident, the suspected shooter remained inside the school after reports of the attack emerged, Arsit Sampantharat, the permanent secretary of the interior ministry, told PPTV. A lockdown at the school was declared over in about half an hour. Images from the scene showed students running with only socks on their feet as they were evacuated from the school. Thailand’s prime minister, Anutin Charnvirakul, has vowed to implement new gun laws, telling reporters only government officials on duty would be allowed to carry guns. However, he did not provide any ⁠specifics, including whether the legislation would tighten gun ownership requirements. Thailand has the highest rate of civilian gun ownership in south-east Asia, and in 2017 the Switzerland-based Small Arms Survey placed the country 13th worldwide for small-gun possession. A number of mass shootings have occurred in recent years in Thailand, including incidents at schools and a large Bangkok mall, and a 2022 attack in the country’s north-east that ‌killed 37 people including 22 children. https://www.mediafax.ro/english/the-magi.text: „The Magic of AUR”: Buzoianu claims that the AUR party „votes for nothing in the judiciary to change” In a post uploaded to Facebook on Friday, Diana Buzoianu wrote about „the magic of AUR, which lies that it is anti-system and then votes so that nothing in the judiciary changes.” According to the minister, at the moment „in the legal committee in Parliament, justice reform projects with the votes of AUR and PSD are being put on the conveyor belt.” What reforms will not be voted on by the PSD? Diana Buzoianu specifies that PSD will vote against reforms initiated by USR. „PSD has put on the agenda the justice reform package initiated by USR and is voting against it. They will vote, for example, against the USR project that demands that the secondments and delegations of judges be made much more objectively so that after years of trials from scratch are not resumed. As was the case with the gift recently given to Negoiță by the Bucharest Court of Appeal,” she wrote. On the other hand, the interim Minister of the Environment says that AUR will abstain from the vote. „AUR is opposing. They will abstain from voting on everything. They have already done this on the first projects in the package. It’s just that they don’t know exactly what they should vote for, the poor AUR people, for example, on a bill that requires judges to no longer be seconded/delegated without clear explanations, thus resuming from 0 trials that have been pending for years with damages of billions or corruption crimes at the highest level,” she continues. However, Buzoianu states that AUR is based on the fact that people do not know that the abstention vote is calculated as a vote for the rejection report, not for the approval report. „In committees, the abstention vote is counted as a vote for the rejection report, not for the approval report. It’s just that AUR relies on the fact that people don’t know these details and leave committees convinced that no one saw them kiss the PSD ring and sell out justice (what exactly should they say).” Buzoianu: „AUR and PSD planned to reject projects today” Buzoianu says that AUR does not have the courage to assume its vote. https://www.stripes.com/theaters/europe/.text: Menu Mobile App Download the app Today's ePaper Read the latest print edition Rewards for readers Archives/Library Subscribe Log in Newsletters Follow Stars and Stripes Facebook X LinkedIn YouTube Threads Europe NATO monitors attacks on commercial ships as Black Sea tensions escalate A NATO flag flies as a Romanian naval patrol boat conducts a demonstration in Constanta, Romania, Aug. 15, 2025. NATO is monitoring recent attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea, including two in Romanian territorial waters. (Regina Koesters/U.S. Army) By JOHN VANDIVER STARS AND STRIPES Published October 15, 2026 · NATO’s top military commander is consulting with defense chiefs as the bloc monitors a string of attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea, including two vessels targeted in Romanian territorial waters, alliance officials said Thursday. U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s supreme allied commander in Europe and head of U.S. European Command, and his deputy are in close contact with allied military leaders over the matter. Consulting one another is “exactly what they need to be doing at this time,” Col. Martin O’Donnell, spokesman for Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, said in a statement to Stars and Stripes. The incidents are the latest suspected drone attacks on commercial shipping near NATO’s southeastern flank, as risks from Russia’s war in Ukraine reach beyond the battlefield. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Thursday that he had met with Romanian and Bulgarian leaders to discuss Black Sea security and that the alliance has strengthened its military posture in the area. Romanian President Nicusor Dan has called for stronger allied measures to protect Black Sea shipping as the investigation unfolds. “We went to NATO, to our allies, and stated that we need equipment to ensure the protection of a NATO state on the Danube (River),” Dan said Thursday, as quoted by Romanian media. “Now we are having the same discussion regarding the Black Sea.” The latest incidents follow a series of drone attacks against commercial shipping near Bulgaria , including attacks that left some sailors dead or missing. The threat has prompted Bulgaria to announce plans to join a NATO counter-drone initiative by the end of October and purchase additional equipment to protect its territory. According to NATO, four commercial vessels were targeted overnight Wednesday and early Thursday. Two of them, the Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Sea Destiny and the Comoros-flagged tanker Yara J, were targeted in Romanian territorial waters, NATO said. A third vessel, the San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader, was targeted just outside Romania’s territorial waters. The fourth, the Tanzanian-flagged tanker Dania J, was targeted in the Danube at the Ukrainian port of Izmail, near the Romanian border. Romanian authorities are investigating the first three incidents, NATO said. The alliance did not identify who was responsible for the attacks or say whether drones struck all four vessels. The incidents coincided with three drone incursions into Romanian airspace near the Ukrainian border that prompted NATO fighter jets to scramble Wednesday and early Thursday. Spanish F-18 Hornets assigned to NATO’s enhanced air policing mission were launched from Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base during an overnight alert, NATO said. Romanian F-16s also responded. That incident followed two other drone incursions on Wednesday. NATO Europe Drones John Vandiver covers U.S. military activities across Europe and Africa. Based in Stuttgart, Germany, he previously worked for newspapers in New Jersey, North Carolina and Maryland. He is a graduate of the University of Delaware. https://www.politico.eu/article/andy-bur.text: LONDON — Andy Burnham laid out his case for reigniting the decade-old Brexit debate at an opulent London banquet Monday, claiming Britain lost more than it gained by leaving the EU. Delivering his first major foreign policy speech at the Lord Mayor’s banquet in London, Burnham said he will sit down with EU leaders following Friday’s U.K.- EU reset summit — where the two sides are expected to sign an agri-food trade deal, link their emissions trading systems, and establish a new system of visas for young people— to work out “options for our long-term relationship.” “This will take time, and we will present those options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next parliament. At every stage, the British people will be the boss”, Burnham said. Advertisement Advertisement The U.K. prime minister set out his ambition to build a closer U.K. relationship with the EU at his first Labour conference as leader in September — confirming weeks later his desire for the U.K. to rejoin the EU within his lifetime. But he is treading a fine line with some members of his own Cabinet, who hold differing views on how far the U.K. should realign with the bloc and whether red lines — including rejoining single market or the customs union — should be crossed. “This is not about re-running the arguments of 2016,” the U.K. prime minister said, while stressing any new arrangement in this parliament will not breach Labour’s 2024 manifesto, must improve the existing Brexit deal, and benefit working people struggling with the cost of living. Lamenting Brexit as “exactly what our enemies wanted,” the British prime minister said the U.K.’s withdrawal from the EU had been the “first domino to fall in a global move towards isolationism and protectionism.” “In the decade since Brexit, our standing in the world has diminished,” he said. “We treated both allies and institutions with insufficient care, and the effects went beyond Europe.” Burnham joked during the speech that it was a stretch talking about the “Makerfield test” — a reference to the views of his Brexit-voting constituents in Greater Manchester — while wearing white tie and having just received a trumpet salute. Advertisement Advertisement Ahead of Monday’s speech, former Conservative Prime Minister Boris Johnson — who signed Britain’s post-Brexit settlement with Brussels in 2020 — warned Burnham against “wasting his premiership” relitigating the European question. “He will impale himself and his party on this point, and he needs to move off it because he won’t win — because the reality is that people are not fools,” Johnson said in an interview with the Telegraph newspaper published Monday . Burnham acknowledged it would “be easier to say nothing about the EU,” but said the hard Brexit deal Britain struck with the bloc ended with “Britain eventually leaving on bad terms, with bad feeling.” “To be frank, we have lost more than we have gained in the last 10 years,” he said, “The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain.” Reform UK leader Nigel Farage — a key figure in the 2016 Brexit campaign — accused Burnham of a “total betrayal” in October when the prime minister prompted speculation he would open the door to restoring freedom of movement. Polling conducted by Ipsos in October found that 56% of Britons would vote to apply to join the EU and 51% said they would support a referendum after the next general election. https://www.bournemouthecho.co.uk/news/2.text: Celebrities Health Nostalgia Bournemouth Anne Diamond visits Bournemouth ambulance station open day Celebrities Health Nostalgia Bournemouth By Ian Crump Group Heritage Writer Share 0 Comments 5 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Anne Diamond swapped television studios for Bournemouth ambulance station at a 1987 fundraising open day. Archive photographs take us back to August 31, 1987, when the station held its first open day. Families and children were invited to look behind the scenes, meet ambulance staff and learn about emergency work across Bournemouth. Anne Diamond was among familiar faces on British television throughout the 1980s. In 1987, she was one of the country's recognisable presenters, and her visit brought a well-known television figure to the event. Anne Diamond at Ambulance open day. August 31, 1987 (Image: Echo) Photographs show Diamond meeting people as visitors gathered at the station. For many, meeting someone regularly seen on television would have made the day memorable. The open day had a clear purpose beyond public interest. Proceeds went to a local spina bifida fund, which eventually raised £1,230. The money helped send children with the spinal condition to Hungary for specialist treatment. That total showed support from local people. It also reflected how community events could bring residents together before social media and online campaigns changed public engagement. Read more: GTA VI set to mark the end of Bournemouth's midnight game launch queues Man discovers 52 new relatives aged 80 after believing his father died in infancy The forgotten wilderness of Canford Cliffs before the millionaires moved in Visitors could see ambulances, equipment and the people behind emergency response work. Such access was unusual and gave families a direct view of a service often known only through urgent calls. The photographs offer more than a record of Diamond's appearance. They preserve a community gathering in late 1980s Bournemouth, including visitors' clothing, the station's surroundings and the equipment used by ambulance personnel. For people who attended, the images may bring back memories of meeting Diamond, exploring the station or supporting the appeal. Some may recognise relatives, friends or former ambulance workers among those pictured. Anne Diamond at Ambulance open day. August 31, 1987 (Image: Echo) Almost four decades later, the archive images record a day when Bournemouth's emergency-service community opened its doors and local people supported children and their families. The event also reflects a time when fundraising depended on people turning out in person. The photographs show how a public open day could connect a local service with residents. They may also help former staff and visitors recall the work carried out at Bournemouth ambulance station in 1987. Were you at Bournemouth ambulance station on August 31, 1987? Did you meet Anne Diamond, work at the station or recognise someone in the photographs? Please contact us with your memories.
